Identifier and correlation practice.

Stable identifiers are convenient and dangerous. An identifier that persists
across contexts allows records to be joined; the same property allows an observer
holding two partial datasets to reconstruct a third.

High-entropy opaque tokens avoid this when they are minted per context and never
reused. A token that is deterministic in a subject, however, is a correlation key
whatever it looks like, and hashing a subject without a secret does not remove the
correlation.

Prefixes leak. A marker of the shape PREFIX-BODY-SUFFIX discloses its family
through the prefix even when the body is random, which is exactly what makes such
markers useful as detectable canaries and useless as anonymisers.
